A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same O3 framework and retain identifiable core experiments. The complete text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original continual-unlearning experiments on ScienceQA, TOFU, and CLINC150, including utility evaluations, component ablations, and appendix experiments with limited retained data.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds original safety, privacy, robustness, scalability, limited-data, and computational-overhead evaluations in its appendices.

M1.justification: The orthogonally regularized unlearning LoRA, contrastive-entropy plus MLM detector training, Mahalanobis/cosine scoring, OCSVM, and soft-weighted inference remain unchanged. The algorithms also match. Glocal-aware scoring renames the existing local-global layer-aggregated mechanism.

E1.justification: Appendices F.7-F.8 add evaluated detoxification and hazardous-knowledge tasks using PKU-SafeRLHF, RealToxicityPrompts, TruthfulQA, and WMDP. Privacy and adversarial test scenarios are also added on existing datasets. The original three task families and their utility datasets remain.

E2.justification: The original seven unlearning baselines and the MDF/Agg detector comparisons retain their membership. Appendix F.11 adds comparison against a reference model fine-tuned exclusively on retained data. Most other additional experiments reuse existing PO and SOPO comparators.

E3.justification: New protocols include five- and ten-request TOFU sequences, paired ScienceQA domains, ten forgetting samples per TOFU request, and a 70%/10%/20% WMDP split. Additional evaluations introduce toxicity scores, membership-inference AUC, oracle-based testing, and attack procedures. Appendix E.1 preserves the original benchmark model and training settings; these additions do not establish rerunning the original experiments.

E4.justification: v2 adds sequence-length and mixed-domain analyses, scarce-forgetting-data tests, membership inference, targeted relearning, adversarial detector bypass, LoRA-rank sensitivity, and explicit baseline failure examples. These substantially expand the questions tested. The original component, regularization, soft-weighting, and retained-data analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix F.11 introduces an output-comparison statistical test against a retained-only reference model, reported through a Truth Ratio-based metric. Its statistical procedure is only briefly described. The original three seeds, numbered 0, 1, and 2, and mean/standard-deviation reporting remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Matched original benchmark, detector, ablation, and limited-retained-data tables retain their numerical values. Substantial new results are added: Table 15 reports membership-inference AUC of 0.559 for O3 versus 0.655 for SOPO at k=10; Table 17 reports second-request WMDP distribution-level accuracy of 12.8 versus 21.5. Further tables add scalability, attack, limited-data, oracle, and rank findings under their respective settings.

T1.justification: v2 Section 2 explicitly separates preservation on retained distributions from a further mutual-information objective for other distributions. It no longer states v1 Section III-B's explicit support constraints covering past and future unlearning requests. The method's mathematical construction is otherwise retained, and neither version provides formal unlearning proofs.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains an OOD-controlled orthogonal LoRA framework that balances continual forgetting and utility preservation without retained data. The new title and revised emphasis do not materially redefine that contribution; the additional experiments primarily extend its supporting evidence.

C2.justification: New Appendix B argues for external blocking as a practical alternative to exact unlearning, discusses open- and closed-model deployment, and leaves secure inference verification as future work. Added discussions address inference/storage overhead and interpret attack resistance and scarce-data performance. Existing RoBERTa/context limitations and retained-data-selection discussion largely move to Appendix H.

D1.justification: v2 adds a source-code URL, a reproducibility statement, and Calflops profiling and storage information. Most existing training details and pseudocode are preserved in Appendix E and Appendix D. Conversely, v1's explicit momentum coefficient of 0.999 and Gaussian/zero LoRA initialization details are omitted, without establishing an implementation change.

R1.justification: The principal unlearning and OOD research positioning remains. v2 adds references supporting targeted relearning, membership inference, detoxification, and sentence contrastive learning. It removes some general LLM background references and v1's cited retained-data-free image-unlearning exception. These are limited substantive updates to the literature context.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled, its abstract and introduction are substantially condensed, related work moves into the preliminary section, and the method components are presented in reverse order. The motivating study and discussion move into appendices, now organized into Sections A-I. This materially changes the narrative structure.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column formatting and substantially redraws the framework illustration. Dataset Tables I-II are merged into Table 7, motivating figures move to Appendix C, and existing tables and algorithms are reformatted. Numerous new experimental tables accompany the added appendix evidence.

improvement.justification: v1's practical continual-unlearning claims relied mainly on short benchmark sequences and component ablations. v2 substantially strengthens their empirical basis through longer sequences, scarce forgetting data, safety tasks, privacy tests, and attacks targeting relearning and detector bypass. Overhead measurements also clarify deployment costs. Some new attack and oracle procedures remain sparsely specified, limiting the breadth of their conclusions, but the added evidence addresses important validation gaps in v1.
